verses.1: When it’s snowing and during the harvest time, it’s not right for a fool to be proud.
verses.2: Like a spider to its web, or like a bird to its nest; thus, the curse of their destruction will be upon them.
verses.3: He who rides on a horse becomes a slave to his desires, and he who rules over others becomes like fools.
verses.4: Do not act foolishly like a fool, for then you will also be punished.
verses.5: Answer the fool like a fool, so that he may not become wise in their eyes.
verses.6: May their feet be bound, so that they may not send anything through the hands of fools.
verses.7: They drink from cups made of fragile materials, and their mouths are like those of fools.
verses.8: As a reminder, just as a stone is placed in the mortar, so too should one give a humble offering to those who are foolish.
verses.9: He was brought before the judge, and he was humiliated by those who were ignorant.
verses.10: He who is able to do all things, and who rewards the foolish and those who work hard.
verses.11: Like a dog that lies down on its back, like a foolish person who acts in a stupid way.
verses.12: You saw a wise man, whose eyes were filled with compassion for the foolish ones.
verses.13: He said, “The rain fell along the roads in those vast lands.”
verses.14: The door will be hinged along its axis, and it will rest on its hinges.
verses.15: Taman tried to pull his hand back into the socket, so that it could be put back in place.
verses.16: A wise man is slow in his actions, because he has twenty taste buds.
verses.17: It holds the ears of a dog; it passes over the grievances that do not belong to it.
verses.18: In her despair, the old woman cried out in pain and agony.
verses.19: For a man who is deceitful, he deceives his neighbor. He says, “I will not play games with you.”
verses.20: In the midst of dead trees, fire will be extinguished; and in places where there is no light, darkness will reign.
verses.21: Firewood for the lamps, and trees for burning as fuel. And men from Midian to make noise.
verses.22: The words of Nirgan were like lightning; they rushed down into the depths of darkness.
verses.23: It’s like gold that’s spread across the surfaces of their lips; it burns and causes evil in their hearts.
verses.24: In his words, he will be deceived; and in his presence, there will be deceit.
verses.25: For John’s voice is not to be believed, because there are seven burdens in his heart.
verses.26: His hatred will be revealed in the assembly; his evil deeds will be exposed in the crowd.
verses.27: It will fall and break into pieces; then it will return to its original state.
verses.28: To a false tongue, one should be resentful; and to a deceitful mouth, one should show rejection.
